page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server instance within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6149 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, with 22 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 instructions. System memory totals 32.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage and requires network-attached block storage, while network throughput is set to a 2 Gbps baseline. There are no discrete hardware accelerators attached.

Benchmark results show balanced mid-tier multi-threaded compute capabilities alongside modest single-core throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 8,278.74 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 7,202.07. Cached small-block read memory bandwidth achieves 402.34 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads drop to 38.36 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates solid in-memory performance with 7.09 million Redis SET operations per second, whereas file compression, database operations, and larger language model inference tests fall into lower benchmark quartiles.

From a resource utilization standpoint, the instance trades off raw instruction per cycle efficiency of newer CPU architectures for dedicated core frequencies and a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Because local storage and public IPv4 addresses are not bundled, operational deployments must account for external storage volume performance. The server fits batch processing, software compilation with Clang, basic microservices, and intermediate Redis caching workloads that require dedicated compute cycles without specialized storage acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.2xlarge is an x86_64 instance from the High Clock Speed family featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores on a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 6149 processor. It includes 32.0 GB of RAM, representing a 1:4 core-to-memory balance, and operates on the KVM hypervisor with AVX-512 vector support. The instance does not include local disk storage, relying on external network storage, and provides a 2 Gbps network baseline with zero attached GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-range performance in multi-threaded compute routines and in-memory key-value processing, reaching 7.09 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside moderate Clang compilation scores. Single-threaded throughput and large-scale data manipulation remain modest. The configuration is suited for intermediate compute workloads, continuous integration workers, application runtimes, and distributed in-memory caching.
